title: A Notion page claims an issue fixed that never actually closed
author: zashiki-warashi
description: The Notion-side twin of release-claims-unfixed-issue and tweet-claims-unfixed-issue: extracts every closing-keyword claim (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses) from a Notion page's own title+body text and checks the named issue's real state. An issue that exists but is still open is the seam: the page is a durable written record that says something was fixed which, in fact, was not. This is the first recipe in the claims-unfixed-issue family to read a Notion page -- notion-page-dangling-reference (ROADMAP.md #2729, the hundred-fifteenth real recipe) opened Notion as a read source for the dangling-reference family, but no claims-* family had a Notion leg until this one. Asks the oath for no new scope: SearchPages and ListIssues both already sit cleared on SCOPES.md's table from that same prior task.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the page's own last_edited_at, holding notion-page-dangling-reference's and issue-comment-claims-unfixed-issue's identical 0.85/0.55 edit-grace-window bar (24 hours) -- not the 0.85/0.5 bar linear-comment-claims-unfixed-issue and slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue use for their own editable surfaces (an existing, pre-dating inconsistency between those two detectors and their own dangling-reference siblings, left alone here -- a separate recipe's drift, not this one's to silently resolve by picking a third number). A Notion page is a text surface its author can still edit at any time, same reasoning notion-page-dangling-reference already gave for 0.55: a claim caught within the grace window may simply not have been fixed yet (0.55, below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden); past 24 hours it is a settled written overclaim (0.85). A claimed issue that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0 -- that broken reference is notion-page-dangling-reference's own seam, not this one's. A claimed issue that IS closed is excluded at confidence 0.0 too, named not hidden -- the claim was true. This recipe only ever checks the issue tracker, not the PR tracker, by design, mirroring the family's existing release-vs-tweet split between claims-unfixed-issue (issues) and claims-unmerged-pr (PRs) -- a future notion-page-claims-unmerged-pr would be the PR-side twin, not folded into this one.
